_comment: Tier-2 for fourc::lubrication#3. The rule holds — a Reynolds solve does return sub-ambient pressure in a diverging gap — but the entry pointed at 'Elrod-Adams' and post-processing clamps when 4C already has the key: LUBRICATION DYNAMIC/PENALTY_CAVITATION, whose DEFAULT IS 0 (off). On upstream lubrication_sb_2d.4C.yaml with the surface velocity reversed, penalty off gives -73.94 (exactly minus the reference) and penalty 1e+08 gives -9.4e-07; no cavitation/vaporisation warning is printed either way and the string 'elrod' never appears. The CONV_NOPEN arm proves the penalty is inert on the converging reference case (result still CORRECT with it off). Verified by execution 2026-08-06 against 4C at /home/alexander/4C/build/4C (2026.2.0-dev, commit 89519cfe76).

_mutation.note: remove the pathology: slide the surface the other way, so the gap converges and no sub-ambient pressure is generated in any arm. SUB_AMBIENT_WITHOUT_PENALTY flips to 'no' and the DIV arms stop failing, so the fixture must go red.
